d: Tannhäuser shrugs up with his head as if he were coming up from a dream. - Venus is pulling him back flatteringly. - Tannhäuser takes his hand over his eyes as if he were trying to capture a dream image

Tannhäuser suddenly stands in a beautiful valley, above it blue sky. On the right in the background the Wartburg, on the left in greater distance the Hörselberg. Right hand leads on half the height of the valley a mountain path towards the foreground, where it then bends sideways; in the same foreground is a Our Lady image, to which a low mountain promontory leads up. From the height on the left one hears the ringing of herd bells; on a high promontory sits a young shepherd with the Schalmei and sings
From the hill on the left, the Landgrave and the singers appear individually in Jägertracht. In the course of the scene, the whole hunting tross of the Landgrave gradually appears on stage.
The singer's hall on the Wartburg; back view of the Burghof and the valley
Wolfram and Tannhäuser appear in the background
The landgrave emerges from a side passage; Elizabeth hurries to meet him and hides her face on his chest
Trumpets. - Counts, knights and noble women in rich ornaments are introduced by noble boys. The Landgrave with Elisabeth welcomes and greets them

Valley in front of the Wartburg, on the left the Hörselberg, - as at the end of the first elevator, only in autumnal colour. The day tilts towards the evening. On the small mountain promontory on the right, in front of the Marienbilde, Elisabeth is stretched out in fervent prayers. Wolfram descends to the left from the woody height.
It is night. - Tannhäuser arises. He wears torn pilgrim clothes, his antlic is pale and disfigured; he wags dull steps on his staff
